abel.title: Abel
abel.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
abel.note: Adam and Eve's second son, and a shepherd. God took his offering, the firstborn of the flock, and passed over his brother Cain's, and that is where the first murder comes from. Hebrews says it was the faith behind the offering, not the offering itself.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

barak.title: Barak
barak.note: He led Israel against Sisera, the Canaanite general, because Deborah told him to, and he would not go unless she came with him. That hesitation cost him the glory of the win.

cain.title: Cain
cain.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
cain.note: Adam and Eve's firstborn, a farmer. God accepted his brother Abel's offering and not his, and Cain killed Abel out of jealousy. God marked him and sent him off to wander rather than putting him to death.

christ.title: Christ
christ.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
christ.note: A title, not a surname. It is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one, and the New Testament gives it to Jesus of Nazareth as the king, priest and deliverer the Old Testament promised. His life and ministry are under Jesus.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

easter.title: Easter
easter.note: The King James has Easter once, at Acts 12:4, and the Greek word underneath it is pascha, Passover. Every later translation says so.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

egyptian.title: Egyptian
egyptian.note: In Acts a Roman officer takes Paul for the Egyptian, a rebel who had recently led an armed rising. Josephus mentions the same man.

enoch.title: Enoch
enoch.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
enoch.note: Seventh from Adam. Genesis says he walked with God, and then he was not, for God took him, with no death notice like the others. Jude quotes a prophecy in his name, and a whole later body of Jewish apocalyptic writing carries it too, though written centuries after him.

esau.title: Esau
esau.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau.note: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin, born red and hairy just ahead of Jacob. He sold his birthright for a bowl of stew, and Jacob later tricked him out of the blessing too, and only after years apart did the two make up in tears. His descendants were the Edomites.

gedeon.title: Gedeon
gedeon.note: The Greek form of Gideon, who beat the Midianites with three hundred men. Hebrews 11:32 has no room to tell his story and just names him with Barak, Samson and Jephthah.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

italy.title: Italy
italy.note: Aquila and Priscilla had just come from Italy when Paul met them, after Claudius threw the Jews out of Rome. Paul later went there as a prisoner, by way of a shipwreck. Hebrews ends with greetings from "those from Italy".

jacob-2.title: Jacob
jacob-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob-2.note: In the New Testament the name mostly means the patriarch, set beside Abraham and Isaac, and Luke's angel promises Mary that Jesus will reign "over the house of Jacob forever". Matthew's genealogy also has a Jacob as the father of Joseph.

jephthah.title: Jephthah
jephthah.note: Son of a prostitute, thrown out by his half-brothers, and leading a gang of raiders when Gilead's elders came begging him to fight the Ammonites. He vowed to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first after the victory, and it was his daughter, his only child. Judges tells it without approving the vow or explaining why he kept it.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesus.title: Jesus
jesus.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
jesus.note: Born in Bethlehem to Mary and raised in Nazareth in Galilee. Around thirty he began teaching in parables, healing, and gathering twelve disciples, until he was arrested in Jerusalem at Passover, tried before the council and Pontius Pilate, and crucified. His followers said he rose bodily three days later, and the New Testament names him the Messiah, God's own Son become human.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

noah.title: Noah
noah.about: Flood survivor living at the time before the Flood
noah.note: God picked him as the one righteous man of his generation and told him to build an ark. His family came through the flood with him, along with pairs of every kind of animal. Afterward God made a covenant with him.

pharaoh-4.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-4.note: The Pharaoh who put Israel to forced labour on store cities. He then ordered the Hebrew baby boys thrown into the river. His own daughter pulled one of them out.

rahab.title: Rahab
rahab.note: A prostitute in Jericho. She hid the two spies Joshua sent ahead, and for that, and for the faith she declared in Israel's God, she and her family were spared when the city fell.

samson.title: Samson
samson.note: He was set apart before birth as a Nazirite, with the rule that his hair was never to be cut, and his strength held as long as the vow did, enough to kill a lion with his bare hands and Philistines by the score.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

sara.title: Sara
sara.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
sara.note: Sarah, spelled the Greek way. Paul and the writer of Hebrews both hold her up as someone who trusted God's promise when she was far too old for it.

sion.title: Sion
sion.note: Another spelling of Zion. The hill in Jerusalem came to stand for the whole city, and in poetry for the place where God lives among his people.

timotheus.title: Timotheus
timotheus.note: Timothy, from Lystra, with a Jewish mother and a Greek father. Paul took him along on his travels and trusted him with hard errands to churches in trouble, and two of Paul's letters are addressed to him.
